name: Tasks
notes: Tasks piles, filters, Asks, the Claude dialog, closing

features.feature: Tasks shows every open thread's open tasks in piles I owe, Owed to me, Waiting for others, Nobody named, with counts, and a folded "Others · N"

A task goes to its pile by owner (me → I owe, a blocked one stays marked), handed over by me (Owed to me), what mine waits on (Waiting, a card per person), no owner (Nobody named), else Others; a pair linked across threads shows once
Order: Due (overdue, then date, then quiet longest), Quiet longest, Thread

The Client filter (the clients with a thread here; a client narrows Thread to its threads and lets go a thread of another), the Thread filter (with counts) and the Who does it filter (Anyone, Claude can do, By hand) narrow every pile and Asks
A pile shows 6 cards then "+ N" / Show fewer

A card shows its title, who (story, blocked by, owner · client, stops T00x), mode icon, thread, also in another thread, due (late in red; a guessed one "from the call / mail / chat of <date>", never late) or "no date", "quiet N d"; the thread's name cut with … on a narrow card
A card opens the task's Details on the right while Tasks stays
Asks (right panel) lists, by person, what they owe late, due within 3 days or quiet 5 days and what my work waits on them for, with their next meeting this week
With no open thread Tasks offers Open Threads; with no task it says "No open tasks"

Send to Claude opens the Claude dialog: the task and its thread, one skill field (Just the task, or skills ranked by fit with "fits best", chosen at once when clearly first; × back to Just the task), a note, Work on it, Yolo (from Today only), Cancel; Escape folds the skill list, then closes the dialog; leaving the view closes it
Work on it types one line (the task's link, the skill, the note) into the Claude panel's session on the thread's AI profile; another profile running or Claude asking something gives a notice instead

Yolo has Claude Code do the task on its own in the background on the thread's profile, run as the folder session (its knowledge and permissions, by the user's one choice 'Claude acts on its own': on, it acts and sends, each change and send listed in its outcome; off, it reads, edits its task and leaves mail as drafts; in both, its own task's thread is all of Echo's threads it reads); the outcome shows above My work, with where each mail draft it wrote is (a run stopped by its 20-minute limit says so); the run reads its thread's brief, people, work and calls, and may change only its own task
Closing a task from Today asks first with an optional comment; the task is done and the comment is in its history
A task's mail shows on it ("Mail sent <date> to …, no reply yet" / "· replied <date>") and, unanswered for 3 days, waits in Waiting for others as "a reply to “<subject>”"

Yolo runs: one list of every Yolo run — on a task and on an item of Needs you now (titled by the item and its subject) — newest first, opened from My work's header and ⌘K (#yolo); each run shows when it started and how long it took, the task (a link opening its details beside the list) or the item, its thread, its state as its outcome says it (working, done, failed — failed at once when another Echo started it — gone, or its pid now another process's —, and always once past its 20-minute limit with its log quiet for 5 minutes), Claude's one line, what it did through Echo's CLI counted (changes, sends, refused; "Nothing through Echo" when Echo noted none, said only of runs Echo followed), its mail drafts, the permissions it ran with (acted on its own, prepared and asked), and Details: each command it ran through Echo and its log (the last 200 KB, said when cut), kept up to date while it works; runs older than 90 days drop off

Yolo runs' filters, in one row above the list (the head and the filters stay, only the list scrolls): state, task or item (each label once), thread, a date range (from, to), changed or sent through Echo, and a search over what Claude said and the title; they add up, a count says how many of all show, Clear resets them, and none matching says so
